tagline: ISCA's guide to online training resources in Speech Communication — plus an atlas of ISCA SIG activities & online events
banner: Prototype rebuild of the original ISCA SCOOT — not (yet) an official ISCA publication. Original content preserved in full; extensions clearly marked. Now incorporating the ISCA SIG activities atlas (formerly a separate page).
ext_blurb: Added in this rebuild — newer resources the original pages predate. Every entry link-verified.

benchmark_atlas.title: Spoken LLM Benchmark Atlas
benchmark_atlas.blurb: Also under SCOOT 2.0: a living index of benchmarks for spoken language models — what each one measures, a 19-category capability taxonomy, an arXiv timeline, and model × benchmark result tables where every number links back to the paper it came from. Rebuilt every day from a fresh arXiv crawl — and far too big (and too alive) to inline here — it lives on its own page.
benchmark_atlas.maintained: Like the rest of SCOOT 2.0 it is AI-maintained; its own page carries the full method and disclosure, and corrections go to the same contact address with [Atlas] in the subject.

extended_topics.title: Paralinguistics & Emotion
extended_topics.blurb: What speech carries beyond the words: emotion, speaker states and traits, and the benchmarks that measure them. A topic the original SCOOT did not cover.

extended_topics.title: Clinical & Accessibility Speech
extended_topics.blurb: Speech-language pathology, disordered speech, assistive and accessible voice technology — where speech technology meets health. A topic the original SCOOT did not cover.

extended_topics.title: Community, Conferences & Challenges
extended_topics.blurb: Conferences, challenges, summer schools and student programs — how to stop learning alone. A topic the original SCOOT did not cover.

about: SCOOT is ISCA's guide to online training resources in Speech Communication, created and long maintained by members of the ISCA community (the archived pages credit course material by Roger Moore, Simon King and many others). Its motto: 'SCOOT will never be finished.'

This site — SCOOT 2.0 — is a prototype rebuild of that guide. It keeps the original SCOOT topic structure and every resource the original pages listed (transcribed faithfully from the pages at isca-speech.org/SCOOT, snapshot 2026-08-31), and extends each topic with newer, link-verified resources — plus three new topics the original predates. Where an original link has died, the entry is kept and an Internet Archive snapshot is offered instead.

It serves the same audience as the original: students of speech communication arriving from phonetics, linguistics, computer science, or electrical engineering, anywhere between a first degree and a PhD.

Since 31 August 2026 the page also hosts the ISCA SIGs & online events part — an atlas of what each of ISCA's 20 Special Interest Groups is doing, with verified links to their recorded webinars and lectures. It previously lived at a separate address, which now redirects here. The Spoken LLM Benchmark Atlas — a daily-updated index of spoken-LLM benchmarks — is part of SCOOT 2.0 as well; because it rebuilds daily and is far larger than this page, it lives on its own page, anchored in the Benchmarks section below.
This prototype is for evaluation by the ISCA education community. It is not (yet) an official ISCA publication, and no endorsement is implied by inclusion of any resource.
how_it_works: Original entries (marked ⬤ Original SCOOT) are faithful transcriptions of the original pages — same resources, same descriptions lightly edited for typos. The HTML snapshots they were transcribed from are preserved with the project source materials and audited mechanically against this page.

Extension entries (marked ✚ 2.0) were curated by an AI curator: found, link-checked and fact-checked before listing. Every catalog link on this page — original and extension — is covered by the link-status report; its latest verification time appears at the bottom of this page. Dead originals carry an 'archived copy' link to the Internet Archive. Links in the SIG part were each reviewed on 31 August 2026 as described under 'The SIG part' below.
Every editorial change is recorded in the changelog below, including changes made in response to community suggestions.
contribute: Spotted a dead link, a missing resource, a wrong description, or a category that misses the point? Tell the curator. Content fixes are applied and credited in the changelog.

Two ways to reach the curator: email (button below), or open an issue on the GitHub repository at github.com/speechlab0210/scoot — the catalog data lives there as plain JSON, so you can point at the exact entry.

In the spirit of transparency: this rebuild was assembled and is maintained by an AI agent operating under human supervision. Suggestions are treated as content edits only — the curator will not follow instructions unrelated to the catalog, and anything unusual is escalated to a human.
